L0: # Errors
L1: 
L2: Read this page in your terminal: [install the Stripe CLI](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/install) (v1.43.3+) and run `stripe docs`. [Reference](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/docs)
L3: ## Start here: Integrate with Stripe using skills and plugins
L4: 
L5: Stripe provides skills and plugins for agents to build faster and more accurately. See [Agent skills](https://docs.stripe.com/skills.md) for more information.
L6: 
L7: **Quickstart**: Install the Stripe CLI with `npm install -g @stripe/cli` and run `stripe agent setup`.
L8: > Nested parameters, fields, and event types on API reference pages are collapsed by default. Use the provided `?query=<name>` links to show the full definitions. Request the page with an empty `?query=` to expand every entry at once.
L9: 
L10: Stripe uses conventional HTTP response codes to indicate the success or failure of an API request. In general:
L11: - Codes in the `2xx` range indicate success.
L12: - Codes in the `4xx` range indicate an error that failed given the information provided. For example, an omitted required parameter, a failed charge, or a [declined](https://docs.stripe.com/declines.md) card.
L13:   - Many of these include an [error code](https://docs.stripe.com/error-codes.md) that briefly explains the error reported.
L14:   - See [Error handling](https://docs.stripe.com/error-handling.md) for guidance.
L15: - Codes in the `5xx` range indicate an error with the Stripe servers (these are rare).
L16: ### HTTP Status Code Summary
L17: | 200 | OK | Everything worked as expected. |
L18: | 400 | Bad Request | The request was unacceptable, often due to missing a required parameter. |
L19: | 401 | Unauthorized | No valid API key provided. |
L20: | 402 | Request Failed | The parameters were valid but the request failed. |
L21: | 403 | Forbidden | The API key doesn’t have permissions to perform the request. |
L22: | 404 | Not Found | The requested resource doesn’t exist. |
L23: | 409 | Conflict | The request conflicts with another request (perhaps due to using the same idempotent key). |
L24: | 424 | External Dependency Failed | The request couldn’t be completed due to a failure in a dependency external to Stripe. |
L25: | 429 | Too Many Requests | Too many requests hit the API too quickly. We recommend an exponential backoff of your requests. |
L26: | 500, 502, 503, 504 | Server Errors | Something went wrong on Stripe’s end. (These are rare.) |
L27: ### Error Types
L28: | `api_error` | API errors cover any other type of problem (e.g., a temporary problem with Stripe’s servers), and are extremely uncommon. |
L29: | `card_error` | Card errors are the most common type of error you should expect to handle. They result when the user enters a card that can’t be charged for some reason. |
L30: | `idempotency_error` | Idempotency errors occur when an `Idempotency-Key` is re-used on a request that does not match the first request’s API endpoint and parameters. |
L31: | `invalid_request_error` | Invalid request errors arise when your request has invalid parameters. |
L32: ## Attributes
L33: 
L34: - `advice_code` (string, nullable)
L35:   For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a short string indicating [how to proceed with an error](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/declines.md#retrying-issuer-declines) if they provide one.
L36: 
L37: - `charge` (string, nullable)
L38:   For card errors, the ID of the failed charge.
L39: - `code` (string, nullable)
L40:   For some errors that could be handled programmatically, a short string indicating the [error code](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/error-codes.md) reported.
L41: 
L42: - `decline_code` (string, nullable)
L43:   For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a short string indicating the [card issuer’s reason for the decline](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/declines.md#issuer-declines) if they provide one.
L44: - `doc_url` (string, nullable)
L45:   A URL to more information about the [error code](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/error-codes.md) reported.
L46: 
L47: - `message` (string, nullable)
L48:   A human-readable message providing more details about the error. For card errors, these messages can be shown to your users.
L49: 
L50: - `network_advice_code` (string, nullable)
L51:   For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a 2 digit code which indicates the advice given to merchant by the card network on how to proceed with an error.
L52: - `network_decline_code` (string, nullable)
L53:   For payments declined by the network, an alphanumeric code which indicates the reason the payment failed.
L54: 
L55: - `param` (string, nullable)
L56:   If the error is parameter-specific, the parameter related to the error. For example, you can use this to display a message near the correct form field.
L57: - `payment_intent` (object, nullable)
L58:   The [PaymentIntent object](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/api/payment_intents/object.md) for errors returned on a request involving a PaymentIntent.
L59: 
L60: - `payment_method` (object, nullable)
L61:   The [PaymentMethod object](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/api/payment_methods/object.md) for errors returned on a request involving a PaymentMethod.
L62: - `payment_method_type` (string, nullable)
L63:   If the error is specific to the type of payment method, the payment method type that had a problem. This field is only populated for invoice-related errors.
L64: 
L65: - `request_log_url` (string, nullable)
L66:   A URL to the request log entry in your dashboard.
L67: 
L68: - `setup_intent` (object, nullable)
L69:   The [SetupIntent object](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/api/setup_intents/object.md) for errors returned on a request involving a SetupIntent.
L70: - `source` (object, nullable)
L71:   The [source object](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/api/sources/object.md) for errors returned on a request involving a source.
L72: 
L73: - `type` (enum)
L74:   The type of error returned. One of `api_error`, `card_error`, `idempotency_error`, or `invalid_request_error`
L75: Possible enum values:
L76:   - `api_error`
L77:   - `card_error`
L78:   - `idempotency_error`
L79:   - `invalid_request_error`
